clusters.name: Live on Stage
clusters.description: Separated on one axis: liveness +2.75 SD (raw 0.72), meaning an audience or room is audible in the recording. Otherwise energetic (0.67) and fairly loud (-8.8 dB), and the longest tracks of any tribe (4:29 on average). Live rock and pop albums (Pink Floyd, Bob Dylan, Queen, The Rolling Stones), long-form filmi and Arabic performances (Umm Kulthum), plus some radio-play episodes recorded in a live room.
clusters.naming_justification: A recording-context tribe rather than a sonic one: the defining feature is where the recording was made, not what was played. Named literally to avoid implying it is a genre.

clusters.name: High-Voltage Anthems
clusters.description: The highest-energy tribe: energy 0.74 (+0.80 SD), loudness -6.9 dB (+0.65 SD), the fastest tempo (139 BPM, +0.70 SD) and almost no acoustic sound (acousticness 0.15, -0.88 SD). Valence and danceability sit below average, so this is drive rather than groove. Rock and metal (38%) and pop (34%) dominate, with the most electronic music of any tribe (9.5%): Metallica, Deep Purple, Black Sabbath, Ramones, Oasis, Armin van Buuren. The most recent tribe (median year 2002).
clusters.naming_justification: Named for the combination of maximum energy, loudness and tempo with low acousticness - the 'electric' end of recorded music. 'Anthems' reflects the loud, full-band or full-mix production, and the lower valence separates it from the brighter Sunlit Grooves.

clusters.name: Spoken Word & Audio Drama
clusters.description: The cleanest tribe in the model: speechiness +4.05 SD (raw 0.87), short tracks (2:29), quiet (-15.6 dB). 85% of its labelled tracks carry a spoken-word genre - German Hoerspiel series (Die drei ???, TKKG, Benjamin Bluemchen, Bibi Blocksberg), Scandinavian barnsagor, audiobook chapters.
clusters.naming_justification: Highest genre purity of any tribe (85%). Named for content type because the cluster is not music at all - it is serialised audio fiction that happens to be distributed on Spotify.

clusters.name: Instrumental Meditations
clusters.description: Defined almost entirely by instrumentalness (+2.63 SD, raw 0.81): tracks with essentially no sung vocal. Also the quietest tribe (-17.2 dB) and the most acoustic (0.83). Dominated by classical (37%) and jazz (28%): Bach, Mozart, Chopin, Beethoven, Stravinsky, plus cool jazz, bebop and modern piano and ambient pieces (Yann Tiersen, Joe Hisaishi).
clusters.naming_justification: Instrumentalness is the single dominant axis, and the low energy and low loudness give the contemplative character. This is the cluster the plan anticipated under exactly this name.

clusters.name: Acoustic Storytellers
clusters.description: Low energy (0.31), high acousticness (0.75), quiet (-12.9 dB), low valence (0.40), but near-zero instrumentalness (0.02) - a singer is present. Vocal jazz, adult standards, lounge, filmi and ballads: Sinatra, Ella Fitzgerald, Billie Holiday, Lata Mangeshkar, alongside modern acoustic ballads (Adele's Someone Like You sits here). Half of all 1950s tracks belong to this tribe.
clusters.naming_justification: The pairing of high acousticness with low instrumentalness means 'acoustic backing plus a voice'; the low valence gives the reflective, narrative character.

clusters.name: Sunlit Grooves
clusters.description: The largest tribe and the happiest: danceability 0.70 (+0.82 SD) and valence 0.76 (+0.81 SD), with solid energy (0.66) and loudness (-8.1 dB) at a moderate 115 BPM. Pop (39%), rock (17%), hip-hop (14%) and Latin (10%): Elvis Presley, Johnny Cash, The Beach Boys, Los Tigres del Norte, S. P. Balasubrahmanyam, and modern dance-pop. Its share grows to 47% of the 2020s.
clusters.naming_justification: Named for the combination of high valence ('sunlit') and high danceability ('grooves'). Where High-Voltage Anthems is fast and intense, this tribe is upbeat and rhythmic - the split the 10 continuous features find in place of the old major/minor pair.
